list: The official 55 trophies, as published on PlayStation and listed by PSNProfiles and Exophase, 2026-11-18
notes: Names, descriptions and grades are the official list, word for word. Every guide is written in my own words for this guide; each one names its source. Hidden flags follow the PSNProfiles listing (28 hidden). Missable means the trophy is tied to one specific story moment or one-time opportunity: earn it during that moment, replay the mission, or keep a manual save from before it.

roadmap.summary: Play the story from Gone Fishing to the final mission. Keep a manual save before each named mission so the mission trophies can be replayed, and grab the partner and one-time moment trophies as their scenes come up.
roadmap.title: Stage 1 — Story first

roadmap.summary: Finish every contact's final mission (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone), complete 8 stranger mission strands across Leonida, and hunt Bret's unique animal.
roadmap.title: Stage 2 — Contacts and strangers

roadmap.summary: Work through the activities: 250 stunts, all Shooting Range challenges to gold, drone races at all 14 spots, 20 race wins, fishing against Cal, one arcade game, meditation at all 18 spots, 50 challenges, bowling follow-through and a melee drive-by.
roadmap.title: Stage 3 — Activities and skills

roadmap.summary: Sweep Leonida: 3 card sets, WAiNK It at 100 spots, 100 vehicles discovered, all 52 areas explored, 5 bank vaults, an armored truck, one illegal operation per gang, all 8 garages, 10 Scooter Bros registrations, plus Combat Focus and the Rhino moments.
roadmap.title: Stage 4 — Collectibles and the open world

roadmap.summary: Launder $250,000 of Marked Bills, spend $100,000 across the shops, mop up the secret and choice trophies, then check the stats for 100% completion and the platinum.
roadmap.title: Stage 5 — Money and cleanup

trophies.guide: The platinum pops the moment the other 54 trophies are all earned, so there is no separate task behind it. Follow the five roadmap stages in order and treat the tracker on this page as the checklist: story first, contacts and strangers, activities, collectibles and the open world, then money and cleanup. The last trophy you need is usually 100% completion or one of the long grinds, so check the stage-5 list when the count stalls.
trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!

trophies.guide: Gone Fishing is the opening mission, so this is the first story trophy and it cannot be earned in free roam. Play through the intro until the mission completes; the trophy unlocks with the mission-complete screen. Because it is tied to a single story moment, keep a manual save from just before the mission in case anything interrupts the playthrough.
trophies.name: Just Like Paradise

trophies.guide: Chapter trophies unlock automatically when the story moves on, so there is nothing extra to do beyond playing the missions of Chapter 1 in order. If a mission fails, retry it from the checkpoint or the pause menu; progress toward the chapter is kept. This one lands when the Chapter 1 finale wraps up.
trophies.name: Paradise Lost

trophies.guide: The second chapter trophy, earned by finishing every story mission in Chapter 2. The chapter structure follows Lucia and Jason as their scheme grows across Leonida, and the trophy pops at the chapter's closing mission. Nothing here is optional, so just keep pushing the story missions marked on the map.
trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money

trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 3 to earn this one. By this point the story is centred on Vice City itself, so expect the missions to move between the city, the Keys and the surrounding towns. As with the other chapter trophies, it unlocks on its own when the final mission of the chapter is done.
trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!

trophies.guide: The last chapter trophy before the finale: complete Chapter 4. The fourth chapter is where the story's threads pull together, and the trophy arrives with its closing mission. If you are tracking the platinum, this is the point to check the missable list — the named-mission trophies from earlier chapters can be replayed, but it is cheaper to catch them on the way.
trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma

trophies.guide: One of only two gold trophies: finish the final story mission. It is the natural end of stage 1 of the roadmap, and it unlocks the post-game state where the rest of Leonida can be cleaned up at leisure. Make a manual save before starting the finale so you can return to the pre-finale world if you want to replay any story moment.
trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off

trophies.guide: Breakfast Run is a named story mission, and this trophy is tied to finishing it. Play the mission through to its completion screen; if it fails, retry from the checkpoint rather than quitting out. Missable only in the sense that it has to be done inside this mission, so if you somehow pass it by, use mission replay from the pause menu to run Breakfast Run again.
trophies.name: Trust

trophies.guide: The Cartel Heist is one of the story's big set-piece missions, and the trophy unlocks when it is completed. Heists in GTA games are multi-part, so follow the planning beats and then the job itself; the trophy only cares that the mission ends successfully. Keep a manual save before the heist in case you want to replay it cleanly for any other trophy.
trophies.name: Break the Bank

trophies.guide: Child's Play is a named story mission; finish it and the trophy pops with the mission-complete screen. Like the other named-mission trophies it can only be earned inside that mission, so if you miss it, replay Child's Play from the mission replay menu rather than starting over.
trophies.name: Family Matters

trophies.guide: Headliners is a named story mission and this trophy is its completion reward. Work through the mission's objectives until the end card appears. The title hints at a fall from grace in the story, so expect a dramatic set piece; nothing in the mission needs a special approach beyond finishing it.
trophies.name: DWNFALL

trophies.guide: VCIA Takedown is the story mission set around Vice City International Airport, and the trophy unlocks when it is done. The airport also matters for the Catch Me If You Can trophy, so while you are in the area, keep an eye out for that one too. Finish the mission and the trophy follows automatically.
trophies.name: Hi-Jacked

trophies.guide: Operation Savage Glory is a named story mission and the last of the mission-specific bronze trophies. Complete it and the trophy unlocks. With this one, every named-mission trophy in the story set is covered; if any earlier mission trophy is still missing, mission replay is the way back, not a new playthrough.
trophies.name: Snow Storm

trophies.guide: The second gold trophy and the long one: reach 100% on the in-game completion stat. In GTA games that stat counts story missions, stranger missions, activities, collectibles and a set of side tasks, and the pause menu's stats screen shows the percentage and what is still missing. Treat this as the final check after the other stages: when the tracker here is nearly full, the stats screen tells you exactly which category is holding the last few percent.
trophies.name: A Long Road

trophies.guide: Pull off 250 stunts in total — jumps, near misses, airtime, drifts and the like, as the game counts them. The count is cumulative across the whole playthrough, so it builds naturally if you drive fast and take jumps whenever you see them. To grind it deliberately, use a fast car on the long highways and causeways around Vice City and the Keys, chaining jumps off ramps and near misses in traffic; the stats screen tracks the running total.
trophies.name: Cunning Stunts

trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Sample every activity type in the game at least once: racing, fishing, the shooting range, drone races, arcade games, bowling, meditation, hunting and the other open-world pastimes the game offers. You do not need to win or finish any of them, just try each one, so work down the activities list in the pause menu and tick them off one by one. The activity icons on the map show where each type lives.
trophies.name: Master of None

trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: There are 42 Shooting Range challenges, and every one needs a gold medal. Go to a shooting range (marked on the map once discovered) and work through the challenge list weapon by weapon. Gold usually means a high score under a time or accuracy bar, so use the weapon the challenge asks for, aim for headshots where they pay more, and replay a challenge immediately when you fall short — the range lets you retry on the spot. This is a skill grind, not a luck one: steady aim beats fast trigger pulls.
trophies.name: The Shootist

trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Top Fun runs drone races at 14 locations across Leonida, and you need a win at each one. The race markers appear on the map once the activity is unlocked; fly the course, hit the checkpoints in order and finish first. Learn each course with a slow first run if you need to — the gates are the same every attempt — then race it properly. A win at all 14 spots is what the trophy counts, not a single race.
trophies.name: Top Fun

trophies.guide: Win 20 different races — different events, not the same race 20 times. Races show up around Leonida as street, off-road and water events; enter each one from its map marker and take first place. A tuned car or bike helps, and the shorter circuit races are the quickest wins. Keep a mental list of which events you have already won so you do not repeat one that no longer counts.
trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos

trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Cal Hampton is Jason's friend and the fishing regular from the trailers, and this trophy is a head-to-head fishing challenge against him. Find Cal at a fishing spot — the Keys are the natural home for it — accept the challenge and out-fish him. Fishing in GTA VI is an active minigame of casting, waiting for the bite and reeling under tension, so keep the line tension in the safe zone and do not rush the reel.
trophies.name: Baited My Tackle

trophies.guide: Find an arcade cabinet — arcades and bars around Vice City have them — and play one game through to its end. Any arcade game counts, so pick the shortest one you can find and finish it rather than chasing a high score. Completing it once is all the trophy asks.
trophies.name: Stick Fiddler

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Andy is one of the side contacts with a mission chain. Play through Andy's missions in order — they appear as contact icons on the map — until the final one in the chain is offered and completed. Contact chains unlock gradually as the story advances, so if Andy's next mission is not showing, push the story forward a little and check the map again.
trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Kenton's mission chain ends with this trophy, and the name points to a boat — fitting for a Leonida contact working the Keys and the coast. Follow Kenton's missions from their map markers through to the last one. Like the other contact chains, the missions arrive in sequence, so finish each one as it appears and the finale will unlock.
trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Billy's chain is the biker one — the name says lone rider — and the trophy comes from its final mission. Ride Billy's missions in order; biker missions tend to involve convoys, rides and turf, so keep a good bike handy. The chain's last mission is the only one that matters for the trophy, but you have to play the earlier ones to reach it.
trophies.name: The Lone Rider

trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Strangers are the oddballs of Leonida, marked with a question mark on the map, and each one has a short mission strand. Complete 8 full strands — not just 8 missions — across the state. Strangers appear as you explore, so this pairs well with the exploration and collectible stages: when a question mark pops up, stop and play that stranger's missions through to their end before moving on.
trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Randy's chain is about supply — moving goods around Leonida — and the trophy is its final mission. Play Randy's missions in order from the map markers. Supply missions often involve pickups and deliveries under time pressure, so use a fast vehicle and a clear route; the finale is the payoff for the whole chain.
trophies.name: Supply & Demand

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Tyrone's chain ends with this trophy — the title is a DJ's taunt, so expect music and Vice City nightlife in the mix. Work through Tyrone's missions as they appear on the map until the final one unlocks. Contact chains can gate behind story progress, so if Tyrone goes quiet, advance the story and come back.
trophies.name: Spin On This!

trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: There are 18 meditation spots scattered across Leonida — beaches, hilltops, parks and quiet corners — and you need to meditate at all of them. The spots show on the map once you are near them or after the activity is introduced; sit down and complete the short meditation at each one. This is a good one to pair with exploration: check the map for unvisited meditation markers whenever you are in a new area.
trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude

trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Bret is the hunting contact, and this trophy is a hunt for one specific unique animal — a named creature, not just any deer or boar. Take Bret's mission, follow the tracking clues to the animal's territory (the wilds around Mount Kalaga and the Grassrivers are the hunting grounds), and take the shot cleanly. Bring a scoped rifle and approach quietly; a spooked unique animal may not give you a second chance on that attempt.
trophies.name: Fair Game

trophies.guide: Collectible cards are hidden around Leonida in sets, and you need 3 complete sets. Cards turn up in shops, houses, hideouts and out-of-the-way spots; the collection screen in the pause menu shows which cards of each set you still need. Sweep each area thoroughly — cards are small and easy to walk past — and use the map markers that appear once a set's cards start showing up.
trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck

trophies.guide: WAiNK It is the in-world tagging activity — leave your mark at 100 locations across Leonida. The spots are spread through Vice City and the wider state, and each one counts once. Treat it as a travelling checklist: whenever you arrive somewhere new, look for the WAiNK prompt and tag it before you leave. The counter in the stats screen shows how many of the 100 you have done.
trophies.name: You WAiNKer!

trophies.guide: Challenges are the game's side objectives — feats of driving, shooting, flying and general mayhem tracked in the pause menu — and you need 50 of them done. They complete passively as you play, so check the challenges list early and steer toward the easy ones first: the list shows your progress on each, and many overlap with other trophies (stunts, races, collectibles). By the end of the other stages, the remaining few are usually the deliberate ones.
trophies.name: One Last Thing

trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: This one needs Lucia and Jason together: build a 4-star wanted level while your partner is with you, then lose the cops and escape. Partner moments happen during story missions and some free-roam sequences, so try it when the two of them are together in the open world. Get the wanted level up with a crime spree, then break line of sight, hide or outrun the search — the trophy pops when the wanted stars clear with your partner still beside you. If the moment passes, wait for the next sequence where you play as the pair.
trophies.name: Hot Together

trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: With your partner alongside, rob three shops in a row without the wanted level dropping between them — back-to-back means keeping the heat the whole time. Pick three shops close together on the same street, rob the first, move straight to the next and keep the wanted level alive; losing the cops or waiting too long breaks the chain. Do it during a story sequence where the pair are together in free roam, and keep a getaway car parked nearby.
trophies.name: Retail Therapy

trophies.guide: Discover 100 different vehicles — getting into a new model for the first time counts as discovering it. Leonida is full of variety, from beat-up sedans in the Keys to supercars in Vice City, plus bikes, boats, planes and trucks. The vehicle log in the pause menu tracks what you have found, so check it when you are in a new area and hop into anything you have not driven yet. Variety is the whole game here: do not just drive one car everywhere.
trophies.name: Whip It Good

trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Combat Focus is the slow-mo aiming mode, and this trophy wants 5 enemies downed in one single use of it. Find a fight with a group of enemies — a gang shootout or a mission with clustered foes — trigger Combat Focus, and drop five before the meter runs out. Line the targets up before you activate it, and use a weapon with a fast fire rate so you are not reloading mid-focus.
trophies.name: Gunslinger

trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: VCIA is Vice City International Airport, and an unscheduled departure means leaving in a plane without a flight plan — steal a plane and take off. Get onto the airfield, take a plane from the tarmac or a hangar, and get airborne; the trophy should pop as you leave the airport's airspace in your stolen aircraft. Expect a wanted level for trespassing, so be quick, and try it during or after the VCIA Takedown mission when you already know the airport's layout.
trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can

trophies.guide: Rhinos are the military tanks, and this trophy is about getting into the heat with one — the description is a nod to being inside the tank while the action kicks off. Steal or commandeer a Rhino, usually from a military base or a high-wanted-level response, and cause the chaos the trophy's joke implies. Once you are in the driver's seat of a Rhino, the trophy follows from using it in the thick of things.
trophies.name: Challenging Tank

trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without any detection — no alarms, no witnesses raising the alarm, no wanted level from being spotted. Go at a quiet hour, move fast once you are inside, and get out before anyone can react. If you are detected, leave and try another store or come back later; the trophy only counts a fully clean robbery.
trophies.name: Sneakthief

trophies.guide: Five bank vault robberies, each one ending with a clean escape. Bank vaults are the big robbery targets around Leonida; plan each one — a fast getaway car, a route away from the cops, and your partner if the job needs two. The escape is part of the requirement, so do not count a vault as done until the wanted level is gone and you are clear. Five vaults, five escapes.
trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal

trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Armored trucks drive set routes around Leonida, and this trophy is a nod to the classic GTA blitz play: stop the truck, crack it open and get away. Ram it or block the road to force it to stop, take the cash, then lose the wanted level that follows. Trucks are easiest to hit on quieter roads outside the city centre, where you have room to set up the block.
trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play

trophies.guide: Explore all 52 areas of Leonida, from Vice City and Vice Beach to the Keys, Mount Kalaga, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia and the Grassrivers. The map tracks which areas you have visited, so open it and look for the parts still fogged or unmarked, then drive or fly through them. This pairs perfectly with the collectible sweeps: visit every area for its cards, WAiNK spots and meditation sites, and the exploration fills itself in.
trophies.name: The Goodtime State

trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: There are 9 gangs in Leonida, and each one runs illegal operations — stash houses, fronts and rackets marked on the map once discovered. Rob one operation belonging to each of the 9 gangs. The operations are scattered across the state, so work through the map region by region and note which gang each target belongs to before you hit it; the stats screen tracks which gangs you have already robbed.
trophies.name: Pest Control

trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Ocean Beach is the Vice Beach strip, and this trophy is a quiet moment: order a cocktail at a beachfront bar and enjoy the view. It is the kind of one-time story beat that can slip past if you rush through the scene, so when the story puts you on Ocean Beach, take the prompt to sit and drink rather than walking away. The trophy pops once the drink scene plays out.
trophies.name: In The Beginning…

trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: A classic GTA moment: drive a car straight through the glass front of a vehicle showroom and out the other side. Find a showroom in Vice City, get a car up to speed on the street outside, and smash through the window in true classic style. It is a one-shot stunt, so line the car up straight and commit — a glancing hit may only crack the glass.
trophies.name: Capital Offense

trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Kolt & Associates runs a bowling alley in Leonida, and this trophy is about the follow-through — the bowling minigame itself. Go to the alley, start a game and bowl; the trophy is tied to the follow-through of a bowl, so play a frame properly rather than just walking in. Bowling is one of the returning pastimes from GTA IV, and the alley is the place to find it.
trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling

trophies.guide: A partnership moment between Lucia and Jason that plays out in front of a crowd — the mass appeal of the description. It is tied to a specific story beat where the two of them do something public together, so play the story naturally and do not skip the scene when it comes. The trophy unlocks when that shared moment lands.
trophies.name: Personal Best

trophies.guide: PlayStation tracks a count up to 500 for this one, and the description is about choices: the decisions Lucia and Jason make along the way. It is a cumulative counter tied to choice moments in the story and the open world, so it fills in as you play through the story making decisions. Because choices are the trigger, do not rush past decision prompts — engage with them — and the counter climbs toward 500 over a full playthrough.
trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder

trophies.guide: Second time's the charm: this trophy is about succeeding on a retry — failing something and then pulling it off the second time around. It is a secret trophy, so the exact trigger is a moment where a first attempt fails and the second succeeds. Play naturally and it tends to come from a failed-then-passed mission or activity; if you are chasing it deliberately, pick a mission or challenge you can fail safely and then clear on the immediate retry.
trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess

trophies.guide: A secret trophy for witnessing something strange — the kind of odd, unexplained event GTA hides in its world. The description's bewilderment is the clue: it triggers on a rare random encounter or hidden event somewhere in Leonida. Explore the odd corners of the map, especially at night and in remote places like the Grassrivers and Mount Kalaga, and keep an eye out for anything that does not fit. It is the sort of trophy the community maps together once the game is out.
trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There

trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: A melee drive-by means striking someone from a moving vehicle with a melee weapon — and bowling them over means knocking them flat. Get a vehicle, equip a melee weapon, and drive past a pedestrian slowly enough to land the hit and knock them down. It is a deliberate, slightly mean trick, so pick a quiet street and a slow pass; speed makes the hit harder to land. One clean knockdown is all it takes.
trophies.name: Ten Pin

trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Marked Bills are the dirty cash from heists and robberies, and contacts around Leonida will launder them for a cut. Earn $250,000 in total through laundering — the counter is cumulative, so every laundered dollar counts. Keep robbing and heisting through the other stages, launder the proceeds whenever a contact offers it, and the total climbs. It is a late-game number, so do not expect it to finish early.
trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar

trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 in total across all shops in Leonida — clothes, weapons, food, car mods, anything that takes money. The counter is cumulative across every shop, so it builds naturally as you gear up, dress the pair and tune cars through the game. If it is the last one standing, the fastest way to finish it is vehicle modifications and high-end clothes, which move big money in a hurry.
trophies.name: Treat Yo Self

trophies.guide: There are 8 garage properties to buy across Leonida, and this trophy wants all of them. Garages go on sale as the story advances and your money grows, and each one is marked on the map when it becomes available. Buy them as you can afford them — they double as storage for the 100-vehicle discovery trophy — and the last purchase pops the trophy.
trophies.name: Little Boxes

trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Scooter Bros is the in-game vehicle app, and this trophy asks you to register 10 vehicles to it. Find vehicles around Leonida — scooters are the obvious ones, but the app takes more than that — open the app on the in-game phone and register each one. Ten registrations is the count, so keep registering every new ride you pick up until it pops.
trophies.name: On the Spot
